questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Combination of travel experience, opportunity to experience nature, a beautiful campus location and a good academic environment

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A beautiful campus location, a good academic environment and lots of freedom to choose courses in English

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Lots (too many) emails. A mandatory orientation event

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The mandatory orientation event was fine, but I felt it was a scam. We were charged $100 USD to attend a 4 hour series of PowerPoint slides with information that was also available through web and email channels. I didn't feel I learnt much new stuff from it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Really hard. Prices in Santa Cruz are insanely high and availability low.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's not easy

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was OK, but I ran into issues with some pre-reqs I had from my home university not being recognized at first. I solved it, but it required some back and forth.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Our undergraduate advisor Lisa was a big help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: No advice

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was a bit lower than back home, but the professors were (mostly) great and it was a pleasure to follow the courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: For the most part, the style of teaching seemed more reminiscent of Danish high school than Danish university.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.answer:
ECON 120 (Development Economics) was great, really dedicated professor.
MATH 117 was super interesting, but very challenging for me as an Econ student - it's targeted at Math majors.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I hoped my Danish travel insurance through Gouda would be sufficient to meet health insurance requirements at UCSC, but it was not accepted - so I had to pay for the much much more expensive UC SHIP insurance offered at campus.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is more expensive, especially housing and insurance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything imaginable.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Personally I really enjoyed going on weekend trips to national parks with the Adventure Rec student club at campus. They also have all the gear you need - tents, sleeping bags, pads, backpacks, water bottles etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on Adventure Rec trips and also plan your own road trips with other (exchange) students to national parks in California, Utah and Arizona. We did two long road trips, and those were my top memories from my exchange stay. Especially Utah has incredible nature. It was necessary to skip classes for a few days to have time for the trips, but it was definitely doable.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was challenging living with a couple of my housemates who made a mess of the entire house and never cleaned up. In general, students in the US are younger and seem to have less experience living on their own.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are friendly and like to smalltalk.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the beautiful location and nature. Go on trips. Enjoy the academics, but don't worry too much about missing a couple of classes to make time for other stuff.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends, both amongst local students and other exchange students - and going on amazing trips with them to experience the unique nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Issues with housemates

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
